TOKYO & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Advasa Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: ADBT) (“ADVASA” or the “Company”), a fintech payment holding company delivering Earned Wage Access (“EWA”) and financial infrastructure solutions, today announced that its Board of Directors (the “Board”) adopted a dividend policy targeting an annual cash dividend payout ratio of 50% for its common stock, beginning with the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

Payout Ratio and Earnings Basis

The target annual payout ratio is calculated as total cash dividends on common stock attributable to a fiscal year divided by consolidated net income attributable to stockholders of common stock for that fiscal year, determined in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP), multiplied by 100. This earnings measure reflects the deduction of amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests, applicable preferred stock dividends and other required allocations. The target does not apply when this earnings measure is zero or negative. The 50% target is based on net income attributable to stockholders, not operating income, and does not represent a dividend yield.

Conditions for Future Dividends

Any declaration, amount, timing and payment of dividends will remain subject to separate approval by the Board, applicable law, including the limitations on dividends under the Delaware General Corporation Law, the Company’s certificate of incorporation, bylaws, any applicable preferred stock rights and contractual restrictions. The Board will consider financial results, earnings, cash flows, liquidity, capital needs, debt obligations, the availability of funds at the parent company, restrictions on transfers from subsidiaries, foreign exchange rates and other relevant factors. The policy is a target and does not create an obligation to declare or pay any dividend. There can be no assurance that any dividend will be declared or paid. Any dividend is dependent upon the Company’s performance, including its financial results, earnings and cash flows, and the other factors described in this release. Actual payout ratios may differ from the target. The Board may modify, suspend or discontinue the policy. No dividend has been declared as part of this announcement, and no per-share dividend amount, record date, payment date or timing of an initial dividend has been established.

About ADVASA

Advasa Holdings, Inc. is a fintech company dedicated to delivering financial well-being to all workers. The company operates an Earned Wage Access (EWA) platform that allows employees to access their earned wages in real time. Leveraging a global patent strategy, it has established a robust intellectual property foundation across markets such as Japan, the United States, and South Korea. By seamlessly integrating with major HR/payroll systems and diverse payment infrastructures, including bank transfers and digital wallets, ADVASA plans to expand into global markets where the demand for financial inclusion is rapidly growing, such as Indonesia and the UAE.

PITTSBURGH, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Viatris Inc. (Nasdaq: VTRS), a global healthcare company, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75%) for the treatment of presbyopia in adults. RYZUMVI is currently approved in the United States for the treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis and is the only commercially available FDA-approved product for that use. This approval expands the product's indications to include presbyopia.

Viatris is exploring the potential for a partner in the United States to commercialize RYZUMVI for the treatment of presbyopia.

About Opus Genetics and Viatris Collaboration
Opus Genetics and Viatris Inc. (through an affiliated entity) are parties to a global licensing agreement which provides for the development of phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% and grants exclusive rights to Viatris to commercialize the product in the United States.

About Presbyopia
Presbyopia is the gradual loss of near focusing ability due to aging, that typically becomes noticeable in the early to mid-40s. It is a nearly universal condition that, when uncorrected, contributes significantly to vision-related disability. Presbyopia leads to symptoms like eye strain and blurred near vision, impacting daily tasks and productivity.

INDICATIONS AND USAGE
RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution) 0.75% is indicated for:

  • Treatment of presbyopia in adults
  • Treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis produced by adrenergic agonists (e.g., phenylephrine) or parasympatholytic agents (e.g., tropicamide) in adults and pediatric patients 3 years of age and older

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings and Precautions
Uveitis: RYZUMVI is not recommended to be used in patients with active ocular inflammation (e.g., iritis).
Potential for Eye Injury or Contamination: To avoid the potential for eye injury or contamination, care should be taken to avoid touching the vial tip to the eye or to any other surface.
Use with Contact Lenses: Contact lens wearers should be advised to remove their lenses prior to the instillation of RYZUMVI and wait 10 minutes after dosing before reinserting their contact lenses.

Adverse Reactions
Presbyopia
The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were conjunctival hyperemia (21%) and instillation site irritation (16%).
Pharmacologically-induced Mydriasis
The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were instillation site discomfort including pain, stinging, and burning (16%) and conjunctival hyperemia (12%). The only non-ocular adverse reaction reported in > 5% of subjects was dysgeusia (6%). The majority of the adverse reactions were mild, transient and self-resolving.

We meet the needs of patients around the world by acting decisively with ingenuity and resolve. Whether we're developing new medicines, working to maintain a resilient supply of needed therapies, or pursuing bold innovation, we strive to deliver solutions that are effective at scale and built to endure. We're purpose-built to make an impact with a broad portfolio that spans generics, value-added medicines, established brands, and innovative medicines that address areas of significant unmet need. HINGHAM, Mass., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HINGHAM INSTITUTION FOR SAVINGS (NASDAQ: HIFS), Hingham, Massachusetts, announced results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Earnings

Net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 was $12,674,000 or $5.76 per share basic and $5.72 per share diluted, as compared to $17,295,000 or $7.93 per share basic and $7.85 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized return on average equity for the third quarter of 2026 was 9.74%, and the annualized return on average assets was 1.11%, as compared to 15.15% and 1.54% for the same period last year. Net income per share (diluted) for the third quarter of 2026 decreased by 27.1% compared to the same period in 2025.

Core net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, which represents net income excluding the after-tax net gain on equity securities, both realized and unrealized, was $11,895,000 or $5.41 per share basic and $5.37 per share diluted, as compared to $8,509,000 or $3.90 per share basic and $3.86 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized core return on average equity for the third quarter of 2026 was 9.15%, and the annualized core return on average assets was 1.04%, as compared to 7.45% and 0.76% for the same period last year. Core net income per share (diluted) for the third quarter of 2026 increased by 39.1% compared to the same period in 2025.

Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $40,968,000 or $18.68 per share basic and $18.51 per share diluted, as compared to $33,833,000 or $15.51 per share basic and $15.37 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized return on average equity for the first nine months of 2026 was 10.86%, and the annualized return on average assets was 1.20%, as compared to 10.07% and 1.01% for the same period in 2025. Net income per share (diluted) for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 20.4% over the same period in 2025.

Core net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which represents net income excluding the after-tax net gain on equity securities, both realized and unrealized, was $33,147,000 or $15.11 per share basic and $14.98 per share diluted, as compared to $22,087,000 or $10.13 per share basic and $10.03 per share diluted for the same period last year. The Bank’s annualized core return on average equity for the first nine months of 2026 was 8.79%, and the annualized core return on average assets was 0.97%, as compared to 6.57% and 0.66% for the same period in 2025. Core net income per share (diluted) for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 49.4% over the same period in 2025.

See page 11 for a reconciliation between United States Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (“GAAP”) net income and non-GAAP core net income. Under changes made to GAAP effective in 2018, gains and losses on equity securities, net of tax, realized and unrealized, are recognized in the Consolidated Statements of Income. In calculating core net income, the Bank did not make any adjustments other than those relating to the after-tax net gain on equity securities, both realized and unrealized.

Balance Sheet

Total assets increased to $4.581 billion at September 30, 2026, representing 1.1% annualized growth year-to-date and a 1.1% increase from September 30, 2025.

Net loans increased to $3.918 billion at September 30, 2026, representing 0.6% annualized growth year-to-date and a 0.1% increase from September 30, 2025.

Retail and commercial deposits were $2.084 billion at September 30, 2026, representing 1.9% annualized growth year-to-date and a 4.7% increase from September 30, 2025.

Non-interest-bearing deposits, included in retail and commercial deposits, were $520.2 million at September 30, 2026, representing 15.0% annualized growth year-to-date and 20.2% growth from September 30, 2025.

Growth in non-interest-bearing deposits in the third quarter of 2026 and over the last two years reflects the Bank’s focus on developing and deepening deposit relationships with new and existing commercial, institutional, and non-profit customers. The Bank continues to invest in its Specialized Deposit Group, actively recruiting for talented relationship managers in Boston, Washington, D.C., and San Francisco. The Bank has also established a dedicated Foreign Mission Group focused on its diplomatic customers, building on several years of growth and experience. This group consists of existing staff, along with new relationship managers who will be joining the Bank in October and November with significant experience serving these clients.

The stability of the Bank’s balance sheet, as well as full and unlimited deposit insurance through the Bank’s participation in the Massachusetts Depositors Insurance Fund, continues to appeal to customers.

Wholesale funds, which include Federal Home Loan Bank (“FHLB”) borrowings, brokered deposits, and Internet listing service time deposits, were $1.930 billion at September 30, 2026, representing a 1.8% annualized decline year-to-date and a 5.0% decline from September 30, 2025, as the Bank replaced these funds with retail and commercial deposits over the last year.

In the first nine months of 2026, the Bank continued to manage its wholesale funding mix to minimize the cost of funds in the current environment, while continuing to replace maturing longer-term liabilities. Wholesale deposits, which include brokered and Internet listing service time deposits, were $514.7 million at September 30, 2026, representing 6.1% annualized growth year-to-date and 1.8% growth from September 30, 2025. Borrowings from the FHLB totaled $1.415 billion at September 30, 2026, representing a 4.4% annualized decline year-to-date and a 7.3% decline from September 30, 2025. As of September 30, 2026, the Bank maintained an additional $957.8 million in immediately available borrowing capacity at the FHLB of Boston and the Federal Reserve Bank (“FRB”), in addition to $366.3 million in cash and cash equivalents.

Book value per share was $235.93 as of September 30, 2026, representing 9.8% annualized growth year-to-date and 11.5% growth from September 30, 2025. In addition to the increase in book value per share, the Bank has declared $3.22 in dividends per share since September 30, 2025.

On September 30, 2026, the Bank declared a regular cash dividend of $0.63 per share. This dividend will be paid on November 12, 2026, to stockholders of record as of November 2, 2026. This will be the Bank’s 131st consecutive quarterly dividend. The Bank has also declared special cash dividends in twenty-nine of the last thirty-one years, typically in the fourth quarter.

The Bank regularly evaluates capital allocation options, including organic growth, special dividends, and share repurchases in light of the prospective return of such options. The Bank received regulatory approval in December 2025 for a share repurchase program of $20.0 million. This approval expires on December 4, 2026. As of September 30, 2026, no shares had been repurchased under this program and the Bank is under no obligation to repurchase shares at all. The consideration of these options may result in special dividends, if any, significantly above or below the regular quarterly dividend.

Operational Performance Metrics

The net interest margin for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 9 basis points to 2.23%, as compared to 2.14% in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. This improvement was primarily driven by an increase in the yield on interest-earning assets, as the benefit of non-interest-bearing deposit growth on the cost of funds was offset by a 1 basis point increase in the rate on interest-bearing liabilities. The yield on interest-earning assets increased by 8 basis points in the third quarter of 2026, driven primarily by a higher yield on loans, as the Bank continued to originate and reprice existing adjustable-rate loans at higher rates, partially offset by a lower dividend on FHLB stock.

The net interest margin for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 increased 49 basis points to 2.23%, as compared to 1.74% for the same period last year. The Bank experienced significant growth in non-interest-bearing deposits and a significant decline in the cost of interest-bearing liabilities when compared to the prior year. This was driven primarily by the repricing of the Bank’s funding sources, as the Bank continued to reduce retail and commercial deposit rates and to take advantage of the inverted yield curve — over most of the last twelve months — by replacing maturing FHLB advances and brokered deposits at lower rates. During this period, the yield on interest-earning assets increased, driven primarily by an increase in the yield on loans, partially offset by lower yields on cash held at the FRB and a lower dividend on FHLB stock.

Key credit and operational metrics were mixed in the third quarter of 2026. At September 30, 2026, non-performing assets, which included three loans secured by real estate and six properties held in other real estate owned, totaled 0.89% of total assets, compared to 0.69% at December 31, 2025 and 0.71% at September 30, 2025. Non-performing loans as a percentage of the total loan portfolio totaled 0.93% at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.80% at December 31, 2025 and 0.81% at September 30, 2025. The Bank did not record any charge-offs in the first nine months of 2026 or 2025.

Non-performing loans and non-performing asset activity included the following during the third quarter of 2026:

  • Non-performing loans at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 included a commercial real estate loan with an outstanding balance of $30.6 million, which is secured by an entitled site for a significant multifamily development in Washington, D.C. and has an associated conditional guarantee from a large national homebuilder and an affordable housing developer. The Bank continues to work actively to identify a resolution that protects the Bank’s interests. The Bank’s allowance for credit losses as of September 30, 2026 includes a $3.0 million specific reserve allocated to this credit.
  • Non-performing loans at September 30, 2026 included a commercial real estate loan with an outstanding balance of $6.2 million, secured by six multifamily buildings located in Washington, D.C. Although the loan was less than 90 days past due, management placed it on non-accrual status as foreclosure is probable. The Bank does not anticipate a principal loss associated with this loan.
  • Non-performing assets at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 included other real estate owned associated with a borrower specializing in affordable housing in Washington, D.C. Following litigation, the Bank obtained two multifamily properties and seven single-family properties in the spring of 2026. All properties were subsequently listed for sale, and the Bank has sold three of the seven single-family properties. The Bank is actively marketing the remaining properties for sale and remains engaged with interested buyers.
  • Non-performing loans at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026 included a small residential real estate loan.

The efficiency ratio, as defined on page 11 below, decreased to 32.81% for the third quarter of 2026, as compared to 37.46% in the prior quarter and 38.26% for the same period last year. Operating expenses as a percentage of average assets were 0.73% for the third quarter of 2026, as compared to 0.79% for the prior quarter and 0.67% for the same period last year. The decrease versus the prior quarter reflects a Fiserv online banking termination fee incurred in the prior quarter. As the efficiency ratio can be significantly influenced by the level of net interest income, the Bank utilizes these paired figures together to assess its operational efficiency over time. During periods of significant net interest income volatility, the efficiency ratio in isolation may overstate or understate the underlying operational efficiency of the Bank. The Bank remains focused on reducing waste through an ongoing process of continuous improvement and standard work that supports operational leverage.

Chairman Robert H. Gaughen, Jr. stated, “Our core returns on average equity and average assets continue to improve materially over time, driven by sustained expansion in the net interest margin through asset repricing and falling funding costs. Growth in non-interest-bearing deposits has been an important driver of improving funding costs and will be a key driver of returns in an environment in which quality loan origination opportunities are more limited and other funding sources remain comparatively more expensive. Both core and GAAP returns remain somewhat below our long-term performance and our expectations for the business, although core returns are approaching acceptable performance levels. Our operational leverage remains critical to generating satisfactory returns and we remain focused on rigorous cost control and continuous operational improvement.

In any given period, our GAAP returns on average equity and average assets may be positively or negatively affected by the performance of our investment portfolio, composed of long-term holdings in financial services and technology companies. Over time, these holdings have contributed meaningfully to growth in book value and we continue to identify opportunities to commit additional capital in this portfolio.

The Bank’s business model has been built to compound shareholder capital over the long term. We remain focused on careful capital allocation, defensive underwriting and rigorous cost control — the building blocks for compounding shareholder capital through all stages of the economic cycle. These remain constant, regardless of the macroeconomic environment in which we operate.”

The Bank’s quarterly financial results are summarized in this earnings release, but shareholders are encouraged to read the Bank’s quarterly report on Form 10-Q, which is generally available several weeks after the earnings release. The Bank expects to file Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) on or about November 4, 2026.

Incorporated in 1834, Hingham Institution for Savings is one of America’s oldest banks. The Bank maintains offices in Boston, Nantucket, Washington, D.C., and San Francisco.

The Bank’s shares of common stock are listed and traded on The Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol HIFS.

(NYSE: DK) (“Delek US”) today announced that the Company intends to issue a press release summarizing third quarter 2026 results before the U.S. stock market opens on Friday, November 6, 2026. A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled to begin at 10:00 a.m. CT (11:00 a.m. ET) on Friday, November 6, 2026.

Investors are encouraged to review the presentation in conjunction with the Company’s earnings press release and webcast. The online replay will be available on the website for 90 days.

About Delek US Holdings, Inc.

Delek US Holdings, Inc. is a diversified downstream energy company with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, pipelines, and renewable fuels. The refining assets consist primarily of refineries operated in Tyler and Big Spring, Texas, El Dorado, Arkansas and Krotz Springs, Louisiana with a combined nameplate crude throughput capacity of 302,000 barrels per day.

The logistics operations include Delek Logistics Partners, LP (NYSE: DKL). Delek Logistics Partners, LP is a growth-oriented master limited partnership focused on owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets. Delek US Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries owned approximately 58.0% (including the general partner interest) of Delek Logistics Partners, LP as of September 30, 2026.

Beauty and wellness routines are increasingly converging, with consumers looking for products that combine visible results, clinical validation and everyday convenience. Research has also found that visible eye redness can influence perceptions of healthiness and attractiveness, creating new relevance for the eyes as part of an overall appearance and wellness routine.3 BRYTLY brings a clinically proven option to this evolving space, by reducing redness and helping eyes look whiter and brighter with results that can last throughout the day, up to 12 hours.

BRYTLY contains no bleaches or dyes and is clinically proven to be safe and effective when used as directed.1 Studies also demonstrated a low risk of redness rebound and tachyphylaxis when used as directed.4-5

“When patients ask about eye whiteners, they want a product they can trust to work effectively and fit into their day,” said Selina McGee**, founder and chief optometrist of Bespoke Vision in Edmond, Oklahoma. “BRYTLY gives Eye Care Professionals a clinically proven option to recommend, with demonstrated safety and efficacy and long-lasting redness reduction from a single drop.”

TEMECULA, CA / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Hop-on, Inc. (OTCID:HPNN) today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Digitalage, Inc., has developed a working pilot console for its AI-assisted news-video infrastructure, demonstrating an end-to-end workflow that moves source material through editorial review, video production, quality control, cataloging and delivery.

The pilot advances Digitalage beyond individual media-generation tools toward a broader operating layer designed for publishers, news organizations, communications companies and enterprises that need to produce media at scale while preserving source traceability, editorial control and an operating record.

Digitalage is building around the full media lifecycle:

INGEST. VERIFY. PRODUCE. REVIEW. GOVERN. DELIVER.

Peter Michaels, Chairman and CEO of Hop-on, Inc. and Founder and Chairman of Digitalage, said:

"This is exactly what I mean when I say Digitalage is infrastructure, not another AI video generator."

"Generating a video is the easy part. The bigger problem is everything around it. Where did the story come from? What source supports it? Who approved it? Did it pass quality review? Can it be changed without rebuilding everything? Where was it delivered? Can you prove what happened?"

"Anyone can push a button and make a video. We are building the infrastructure behind the button."

THREE PATHS FROM SOURCE TO VIDEO

The current pilot demonstrates three distinct production workflows.

The first allows an authorized user to provide source text and produce a video using an AI presenter.

The second allows incoming feed content to trigger production automatically through configurable rules, allowing those rules to determine whether material proceeds through the workflow without manual intervention.

The third provides an editorially controlled path in which a proposed script is checked against its underlying source material and held for human approval before rendering begins.

Together, those workflows are intended to allow organizations to automate routine production without surrendering editorial authority when human review is required.

AN OPERATING SYSTEM AROUND THE MEDIA

The working pilot brings multiple production, editorial and governance functions into a unified console.

Capabilities demonstrated by the Digitalage development team include:

  • Source-text and feed-based story ingestion
  • AI-presenter video generation
  • Rule-based automated processing
  • Source-to-script editorial review
  • Human approval before rendering
  • A 14-stage rendering workflow
  • A 71-check video quality report
  • Story and editorial management
  • Feed and automation-rule management
  • Media cataloging
  • Reusable brand kits
  • Signed webhook delivery
  • Per-run API capability validation and usage tracking

The system currently includes 87 working API capabilities.

The console tracks which capabilities are exercised and validated during each individual workflow run. Accordingly, a display such as "4 of 87" reflects the number of capabilities used or validated in that specific run, not the number of capabilities available or functioning across the system.

Automated testing, engineering review, improvements and bug fixes continue across the platform.

Digitalage is developing the architecture as a multi-vendor environment rather than one dependent on a single AI model or provider.

The objective is infrastructure capable of orchestrating the tools each workflow requires.

AUTOMATION WITHOUT REMOVING ACCOUNTABILITY

Digitalage believes artificial intelligence will dramatically increase the speed and volume at which media can be created.

The company also believes greater automation makes provenance, source traceability, editorial controls and auditable production processes more important, not less.

The Digitalage architecture is being designed so routine workflows can be automated while organizations retain human approval where editorial policy requires it.

The system is also being developed to preserve underlying source material and production state so changes can be made within the workflow rather than forcing an editor to rebuild an entire production from the beginning.

Robert T. Braun, CEO of Digitalage, said:

"Enterprise customers do not simply need another tool that can generate content. They need reliability, repeatability, governance, control and an operating record."

"As these systems scale, the value is not simply in creating another piece of media. It is in maintaining the source, rights, editorial decisions, production state and delivery history around that media."

"That is what turns a collection of AI tools into enterprise infrastructure."

THE MEDIA KEEPS ITS HISTORY

Most generative tools are designed to produce an output.

Digitalage is being developed around a different model:

The finished media should retain an operating record of how it came into existence.

That record is designed to include the underlying source material, script development, editorial decisions, approval state, production stages, quality review, catalog identity and delivery history.

The objective is to allow an organization to know not only what was published, but also how it got there.

That distinction becomes increasingly important as organizations move from manually producing individual pieces of content to using artificial intelligence and automation to produce media at scale.

Michaels said:

"A finished video should not become a dead file the moment it is rendered."

"We want the source, the decisions, the approvals, the production history and the delivery record to remain connected to the media."

"Most AI tools give you an output. We are building infrastructure that remembers how the output was created."

ONE INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER ACROSS THE MEDIA LIFECYCLE

The news-video console is part of a broader Digitalage architecture being developed across live broadcasting, replay, recorded media, creator monetization, moderation, provenance, searchable catalogs, AI-assisted publishing, rights-aware workflows and enterprise licensing.

Digitalage is also being designed to work alongside production tools creators already use.

Rather than requiring creators to abandon established broadcasting workflows or audiences, Digitalage is designed to accept streams through workflows compatible with production environments such as OBS.

The strategy is straightforward:

CREATORS SHOULD NOT HAVE TO START OVER SIMPLY TO ADD DIGITALAGE.

OBS functions as a production control room where creators can manage cameras, audio and graphics before sending a live stream to an audience.

Digitalage's stream-key workflow is designed to allow creators to add Digitalage alongside existing broadcast channels rather than requiring them to replace those channels.

Digitalage's creator application, currently in testing, connects multiple portions of this lifecycle, including live broadcasting, replay, timed interaction, catalogs and access-pass payment functionality.

When a live event ends, the Digitalage model is designed to continue.

The live stream can become a replay.

The replay can become part of the creator's catalog.

Conversation can remain connected to the moment that created it.

The resulting media can continue creating opportunities for discovery, access and monetization.

The same architectural philosophy now extends into news production.

A story can begin as source material, move through structured editorial and production stages, become finished media and enter a persistent catalog rather than existing only as a one-time AI render.

Digitalage summarizes the model with a simple principle:

"Live is the moment. The catalog is the business."

FROM WORKING PILOT TO COMMERCIAL DEPLOYMENT

With the core workflow now demonstrated, Digitalage's next phase is focused on converting the pilot into deployable enterprise infrastructure.

Current work includes production hardening, performance testing, determining finished-media production costs, configuring customer-specific workflows, establishing pricing and finalizing commercial billing architecture for the newsroom product.

The current news-video pilot operates on a local development stack, and certain production components remain under continuous review, testing and development.

Digitalage is not announcing commercial revenue or a completed customer deployment from the newsroom pilot at this time.

The company intends to demonstrate the system to prospective publishers, news organizations, communications companies and enterprise customers as development reaches the appropriate stage.

Signed commercial agreements and deployments will be announced when and if they are finalized.

The objective is now to move from demonstrated technology to controlled commercial deployment.

DIGITALAGE: NOT A PLATFORM. INFRASTRUCTURE.

Digitalage's development work now spans multiple interconnected layers of the media lifecycle, including live broadcasting, replay, VOD, creator access and monetization, moderation, content processing, searchable media, AI-assisted production and enterprise workflows.

Rather than developing isolated applications for each media format or tying the company's future to a single artificial-intelligence provider, Digitalage is pursuing an infrastructure model in which live, recorded, human-created and AI-assisted media can operate through a shared underlying architecture.

Michaels concluded:

"We spent years building pieces of this architecture. Now those pieces are beginning to work together."

"Live. Replay. Verification. Moderation. News production. Rights. Delivery. Monetization."

"Not a platform. Infrastructure."

ABOUT HOP-ON, INC.

Hop-on, Inc. (OTCID: HPNN) is a publicly traded technology company and the parent company of Digitalage, Inc.

Through Digitalage, the company is developing stateful media infrastructure for live and recorded content, creator media, publishing workflows, provenance, content governance, searchable catalogs, rights-aware distribution and monetization.

For more information, visit Digitalage.com.

NORTH EAST, PA / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / NFI Empire, a fully owned subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc. (OTCID:NWPG), today announced that American Force Wheels has joined Project Reborn-001 as a key partner. The custom vehicle build is heading to auction at The Red Bird Games in Brentwood, TN, with proceeds benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. American Force is supplying custom forged N33 Barrage DRW wheels that will be wrapped in 37x13.50R22 tires, giving the one-of-one dually its bold, purpose-driven stance.

Rendering of Project Reborn-001, the 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab dually, rolling on American Force forged wheels.

The Build Update

Project Reborn-001 continues its transformation of a 1979 Chevrolet K30 crew cab into a modern performance powerhouse, pairing the classic square-body exterior with a contemporary GMC Sierra 3500 frame, Duramax diesel drivetrain, suspension, and amenities. American Force Wheels has contributed its N33 Barrage wheels in 22-inch DRW (dual rear wheel) configuration. The N33 Barrage is part of American Force's forged monoblock aluminum lineup, engineered for strength and reduced weight while delivering the aggressive styling expected of a high-end custom dually. These wheels will be wrapped with 37x13.50R22 tires, completing the truck's unmistakable ground-pounding presence as it prepares for SEMA and its live auction benefiting The Brett Boyer Foundation. Consistent progress updates will continue to be shared as the build advances.

American Force N33 Barrage forged wheel mounted with a 37x13.50R22 tire.

The N33 Barrage forged monoblock aluminum wheel in a polished finish.

"Project REBORN represents what the automotive community can accomplish when great companies come together behind an even greater purpose," said Jason Sandusky of American Force Wheels. "We're proud to support NFI Empire and The Brett Boyer Foundation and to put American Force wheels on a build that will ultimately help children and families affected by congenital heart disease. REBORN-001 is going to be an incredible truck, but knowing what it represents and the impact it can make is what makes being part of this project truly special."- Jason Sandusky, Marketing / Event / Partnership Management, American Force

"Partnering with American Force Wheels on Project Reborn-001 brings American-made forged strength and style that perfectly complement the performance and purpose of this extraordinary build," said Justin Fried, CEO of Newport Gold, Inc. and NFI Empire. "Every component on this truck exists to amplify awareness and funding for The Brett Boyer Foundation's work against congenital heart disease and in celebration of the Down syndrome community."

What is The Brett Boyer Foundation

The Brett Boyer Foundation is a Nashville, Tennessee-based nonprofit charitable organization founded in 2017 by Ellen and Bo Boyer in loving memory of their daughter, Sadie Brett Boyer, who was diagnosed prenatally with Down syndrome and a congenital heart defect. Sadie Brett may have only lived for 7 months, but her impact has reached countless children and families, ultimately changing the medical industry by providing kids an edge and fighting chance against CHD. Congenital heart disease (CHD) is one of the most common conditions affecting infants and one that remains severely underfunded compared to other childhood illnesses. The Brett Boyer Foundation is dedicated to raising awareness and funding research aimed at advancing treatment options while providing support to families and providers navigating a CHD diagnosis. Another mission of The Brett Boyer Foundation is to celebrate the love, capability, and dignity of the Down syndrome community. 50% of babies born with Down syndrome fight CHD. Through fundraising efforts and partnerships with like-minded organizations both in the Nashville area and across the United States, the Foundation works to improve outcomes for children living with heart disease so that fewer families endure the loss the Boyers experienced.

The Brett Boyer Foundation: https://www.thebrettboyerfoundation.org/

About American Force Wheels

American Force Wheels is a leading manufacturer of premium forged aluminum wheels for trucks, Jeeps, SUVs, and UTVs. Founded with a commitment to American-made quality, the company designs, engineers, machines, and finishes its wheels in-house at a state-of-the-art facility. Specializing in both single rear wheel and dual rear wheel (DRW) applications, American Force is known for monoblock forged construction that delivers exceptional strength, reduced weight, and bold styling. Every wheel is backed by a lifetime structural warranty. Learn more at https://www.americanforce.com/.

About NFI Empire

NFI Empire (NFIEmpire.com) is the wholly owned operating subsidiary of Newport Gold, Inc., a North East, Pennsylvania-based custom automotive company known for exclusive builds, high-performance vehicles, and deep technical and digital expertise across both traditional and digital automotive sectors. The Company has ceased all mining-related operations; Newport Gold is now a holding company whose operations are conducted entirely through NFI Empire. NFI Empire's stated goal is to become the first publicly traded automotive enthusiast company to integrate a brick-and-mortar business model with a proprietary technology platform.

Grosse Pointe, Michigan, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Broad Arrow Auctions and Private Sales, driven by Hagerty (NYSE: HGTY), is at the forefront of the modern Ferrari collector market as it continues to show significant growth in 2026. Analysis from Hagerty shows a surge in demand for modern supercars which now account for 38 percent of the global collector car auction market. Hypercars have seen a similar increase, representing 32 percent of the auction market, with both segments being driven in large part by the demand for highly desirable Ferrari models.

Broad Arrow Auctions has released another highly desirable lineup of Ferrari hypercars and supercars for its upcoming second annual Las Vegas Auction, set for October 31 in partnership with Concours at Wynn Las Vegas.

Latest highlights are led by a 2025 Ferrari Daytona SP3 (Estimate: $16,000,000 - $18,000,000), chassis number 314846, finished in the exquisite Tailor Made shade of Verde Francesca over a two-tone Nero Alcantara and Mustard Aunde Jeans interior. Offered from its original owner, the curator of an exceptional private collection, the SP3 is one of just 600 examples produced and displays just 81 miles at cataloging. The second model in Ferrari’s sought after “Icona” series, the Daytona SP3 is many things—a rolling tribute to one of the marque’s most triumphant afternoons, a showcase of naturally aspirated engineering at its peak, and quite possibly the final chapter in a mid-engine, naturally aspirated lineage that began nearly sixty years ago. The car on offer is equipped with numerous carbon fiber elements, airbrushed fender shield, a suspension lifter, and a full complement of factory accessories.

“The collector car market has quickly recognized the significance of the Daytona SP3 in Ferrari’s history,” says Barney Ruprecht, Vice President of Auctions for Broad Arrow. “In the few short years since the SP3's reveal, values have climbed sharply, reflecting both the model's extreme exclusivity, and a growing understanding that it may represent the final expression Ferrari’s naturally aspirated V12 for the road. 2014 Ferrari LaFerrari (Estimate: $8,500,000 - $10,000,000)

This is a low-mileage, extensively specified example of the first hybrid hypercar from Maranello, producing a combined 950 horsepower from its 6.3-liter V12 hybrid powerplant. FDA expands the approved use of phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% to include age-related near vision impairment, which affects millions of adults in the United States

Approval supported by positive results from pivotal Phase 3 VEGA-2 and VEGA-3 trials, which met primary and all key secondary efficacy endpoints

RESEARCH TRIANGLE PARK, N.C., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Opus Genetics, Inc. (Nasdaq: IRD) (“Opus Genetics” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing gene therapies to restore vision and prevent blindness in patients with inherited retinal diseases (IRDs), today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Company’s supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) for phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% for the treatment of presbyopia in adults.

Opus Genetics and Viatris Inc. (through an affiliated entity) are parties to a global licensing agreement which provides for the development of phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% and grants exclusive rights to Viatris to commercialize the product in the United States.

This FDA approval in presbyopia will trigger a milestone payment to Opus Genetics.

Presbyopia is an age-related condition that affects the ability to focus on near objects, often requiring reading glasses or other corrective lenses. The condition affects approximately 90% of adults in the United States over the age of 45. Phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% offers a non-invasive, pharmacologic treatment option designed to improve near vision while preserving distance vision.

“This approval marks an important milestone for Opus Genetics, representing our second U.S. drug approval and underscoring our clinical and regulatory capabilities,” said George Magrath, M.D., Chief Executive Officer, Opus Genetics. “It reinforces our commitment to advancing innovative ophthalmic therapies that address unmet patient needs. We are grateful to the patients, investigators and clinical sites who contributed to this achievement, and we look forward to working closely with our commercial partner to bring RYZUMVI® to patients.”

The FDA approval is supported by positive results from the pivotal Phase 3 VEGA-2 and VEGA-3 clinical trials, both of which met their primary and all key secondary efficacy endpoints, with no treatment-related serious adverse events reported. Phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% is a preservative-free, topical formulation that reduces pupil diameter through a sympatholytic mechanism of action, without engaging the ciliary muscle.

Phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% is marketed in the United States as RYZUMVI® for the treatment of pharmacologically induced mydriasis. The supplemental approval expands its approved indications to include presbyopia in adults.

INDICATIONS AND USAGE

RYZUMVI® (phentolamine ophthalmic solution) 0.75% is indicated for:

  • Treatment of presbyopia in adults
  • Treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis produced by adrenergic agonists (e.g., phenylephrine) or parasympatholytic agents (e.g., tropicamide) in adults and pediatric patients 3 years of age and older

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings and Precautions

Uveitis: RYZUMVI is not recommended to be used in patients with active ocular inflammation (e.g., iritis).

Potential for Eye Injury or Contamination: To avoid the potential for eye injury or contamination, care should be taken to avoid touching the vial tip to the eye or to any other surface.

Use with Contact Lenses: Contact lens wearers should be advised to remove their lenses prior to the instillation of RYZUMVI and wait 10 minutes after dosing before reinserting their contact lenses.

Adverse Reactions

Presbyopia

The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were conjunctival hyperemia (21%) and instillation site irritation (16%).

Pharmacologically-induced Mydriasis

The most common ocular adverse reactions reported in > 5% of subjects were instillation site discomfort including pain, stinging, and burning (16%) and conjunctival hyperemia (12%). The only non-ocular adverse reaction reported in > 5% of subjects was dysgeusia (6%). The majority of the adverse reactions were mild, transient and self-resolving.

Please see complete Prescribing Information

About Phentolamine Ophthalmic Solution 0.75%

Phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% is a non-selective alpha-1 and alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist to reduce pupil size, administered as an eye drop. It works by blocking alpha-1 adrenergic receptors on the iris dilator muscle. Phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% is designed to reduce pupil diameter through a sympatholytic mechanism of action that avoids engaging the ciliary muscle. Phentolamine ophthalmic solution 0.75% is currently approved in the U.S. for the treatment of pharmacologically-induced mydriasis produced by adrenergic agonists (e.g., phenylephrine) or parasympatholytic (e.g., tropicamide) agents; and has successfully completed a Phase 3 program for presbyopia (VEGA clinical program), and is being evaluated in a Phase 3 program for the treatment of dim (mesopic) light vision disturbances (sometimes referred to as DLD) after keratorefractive surgery (LYNX clinical program).
